This in turn puts a substantial dent in actuarial science’s ability to calculate accurate premiums for these activities.

key_points.point: The document emphasizes the fundamental opacity of deep neural networks, noting that weighted connections across multiple layers are rarely known or traceable outside the black box. This structural feature prevents both creators and users from fully understanding the internal justifications of AI decisions, creating severe accountability gaps when harm occurs. From a safetyist perspective, this uninspectable nature confirms that AI errors and unpredictable behaviors stem from deep architectural constraints rather than easily fixable software bugs.
key_points.verbatim: The weight of these connections is determined by the AI algorithm and is rarely known or traceable outside of the black-box, in which the process takes place. The more layers a neural network has, the more difficult it is to fully understand and predict the weight assigned to each neuron and, as a result, the outcome of the AI entity itself. Given these unique features of the black-box, neither the users nor the creators can fully understand the process and justification which form the basis of an AI decision-making process.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Multi-layered neural networks operate as uninspectable black boxes where internal weight assignments remain untraceable, preventing human understanding of decision justifications.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within safetyist discourse that multi-layered neural networks operate as uninspectable black boxes whose internal weight assignments prevent human understanding of decision justifications. Encompasses: Neural network opacity, untraceable weight connections, decision-making inscrutability.
